title: A new sequence under a key uses the step of the mapping it is added to, not the step of an earlier mapping
notes: The document has two nested block mappings with different steps: `x` indents its entry four spaces under its key, and `z`, the mapping the new key is added to, indents its entry two. The patch adds `/z/n` with the sequence `[1]`; there is no sibling sequence to copy. The specification allows any indentation of the dash greater than the key's, so the bytes rest on a kit convention (docs/edit-semantics.md): the step is taken from the mapping the new key belongs to, here two spaces, so `n` is written at column 2 and its dash at column 4 (`    - 1`). A step of four, taken from the earlier mapping, would put the dash at column 6 and fails the case. The new member goes at the end of `z`, which is a second convention (RFC 6902 does not fix the position). The case carries the tag `convention`. The result reads back as `x` with `y` 1, and `z` with `w` 1 and `n` a sequence of the single item 1.
